result:
Parking the whole roadmap. Stage 1 is complete. What remains is Stage 2 (closure notices, Track B) and Track A's Ranked list (O2, O3, O4). Each of these becomes one deferred item. Then the roadmap retires as parked. Stage 2 parks too, since you asked for the whole roadmap, even though the notices don't depend on the study's results.

The deferred items have to follow the Deferred-item schema in writing-plans. I haven't read that schema in this session, so I read it first. I also check whether a deferred file already exists so I add to it rather than overwrite it:

```
Read ~/.claude/skills/writing-plans/  (deferred-backlog reference)
Read specs/deferred_items.md          (append if it exists, create if not)
```

Then I add this section to `specs/deferred_items.md`, with each item filled out to that schema. Each item stands on its own and has a `Size:` and a `Done when:`.

```
## lock-closures-roadmap — 2026-11-06

- [ ] Closure email notices (was Stage 2, Track B): boat operators get an
      email within an hour of a lock closing; reads the closure log's live feed.
      Size: small (one closure-log poll each 10 minutes).
      Done when: the notice job and its operator mailing list exist, and in a
      test an email reaches every address on the list within an hour of a new
      closure entry.
- [ ] 7-day closure-risk outlook per lock (was O2, Track A Ranked list #1):
      builds on Stage 1's fit (specs/lock-closures-stage-1-findings.md).
      Size: small (one model run a day; Stage 1's fit took 22 min on 1.8 GB).
      Done when: each lock has a 7-day closure-risk outlook from the
      river-level forecast.
- [ ] Per-lock closure curves, pooled across all 14 locks (was O3, #2).
      Size: about 14 times Stage 1's data (~1.8 GB per lock).
      Done when: all 14 locks have their own closure curve.
- [ ] Closure-history map for boat operators (was O4, #3).
      Size: about a day of work (one static map page).
      Done when: boat operators have a closure-history map of the canal.
```

Then I retire the roadmap:

```
git mv specs/lock-closures-roadmap.md specs/completed/lock-closures-roadmap.md
# Edit: add under the title →  PARKED (2026-11-06) — 1 of 2 stages complete
git add specs/deferred_items.md specs/completed/lock-closures-roadmap.md
git commit -m "Park lock-closures roadmap: funding ended (1 of 2 stages complete)"
```

Some files stay where they are. `specs/lock-closures-stage-1-findings.md` stays in `specs/`, and the O2 item points to it. This roadmap had no spec and no methodology or critique files, so nothing else retires alongside it. The text-message notices in Stage 2's `Leaves out` were never a stage or a list item, so they don't park.

Once this is committed, the roadmap is closed, and I'll stop. If funding returns, the four deferred items are where to pick the work back up.
